intended_object: The real Kalton–Peck space Z₂: pairs (w, x) of real sequences with x ∈ ℓ₂ and w − Ω(x) ∈ ℓ₂, where Ω is the Kalton–Peck centralizer x ↦ 2x·log(|x|/‖x‖₂) (scaled by 2 here). Inferred from the docstring and from the target `CanonicalRealKaltonPeck`.
explanation: `KP` is only a local abbreviation for `CanonicalRealKaltonPeck`, as its docstring says. That type, defined in Support/Coordinates.lean, is the subtype {p : (ℕ → ℝ) × (ℕ → ℝ) // p.2 ∈ ℓ₂ ∧ p.1 − centralizer p.2 ∈ ℓ₂}, with centralizer x n = 2·xₙ·log(|xₙ|/‖x‖₂). This is the standard presentation of the Kalton–Peck twisted Hilbert space Z₂. The factor 2 is a normalization that comes from complex interpolation. Rescaling the first coordinate by 1/2 matches it with the version without the factor, so it is the same space up to a canonical isomorphism. The convention log 0 = 0 deals with zero coordinates and with x = 0 in the usual way. Z₂ is a specific space defined on sequences indexed by ℕ, so there is no question of generality. Mathlib has no Kalton–Peck space. The alias adds nothing of its own, and the object it names matches the literature.
